domain: road trip food packing for a group
base_instruction: You are a helpful trip planning assistant. Help the user figure out what food and snacks to pack for a group road trip. Track who is going, any dietary needs, and help evaluate specific food items when asked. When the group or their needs change, adjust your recommendations accordingly.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're doing a road trip this Saturday — about 6 hours of driving. I need help figuring out what food to pack for the car.

flow_info.value: Four people going: me, Derek, Priya, and Sam
Derek was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
About 6 hours of driving, leaving early morning
We have a cooler so cold stuff is fine
My sister Maya is joining us now, so five people total

Sam's girlfriend just texted me — she said Sam went to the allergist last week and it turns out it's not lactose intolerance, it's actually a full milk protein allergy. Apparently even whey and casein set him off
Derek just bailed on us — his kid is sick so he's staying home. He asked if we could drop off some snacks at his place on the way out though since he was looking forward to it
Priya eats everything, no restrictions at all
Snack list to check: trail mix with almonds and dark chocolate, string cheese sticks, rice crackers with hummus, whey protein bars, sourdough pretzels

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, or eggs — strict vegetarian
constraints.surface_form: Priya grew up in a Jain household and still follows it pretty strictly
inference_chain: Strict Jain → vegetarian (no meat, no fish, no eggs)
Also traditionally avoids root vegetables but 'pretty strictly' implies standard vegetarian at minimum

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or cross-contaminated products
constraints.surface_form: Derek was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye

constraints.value: Initially stated as lactose intolerant — cannot digest lactose in dairy
Full milk protein allergy — cannot have any dairy protein including whey and casein, not just lactose
constraints.surface_form: Sam's girlfriend just texted me — she said Sam went to the allergist last week and it turns out it's not lactose intolerance, it's actually a full milk protein allergy. Apparently even whey and casein set him off
Maya carries an EpiPen everywhere because of a peanut scare she had as a kid
inference_chain: Peanut scare as a kid → peanut allergy
Carries EpiPen → allergy is serious/anaphylactic level

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a road trip with friends. You will introduce the group and their dietary issues, then updates will happen: your sister Maya joins (she has a peanut allergy implied by her EpiPen), Sam's constraint gets upgraded from lactose intolerance to full milk protein allergy, and Derek drops out but wants snacks dropped off. At the end you will ask the assistant to check a specific snack list. You never tell the assistant what the correct answers are.

You are a calm, easygoing trip organizer. You relay updates from friends in third person ('Sam's girlfriend texted me...', 'Derek just told me...'). You never express frustration even when plans change. Everything is normal coordination among friends.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: string cheese has milk protein (Sam), whey protein bars have whey (Sam milk protein allergy), sourdough pretzels contain gluten (problematic ONLY for Derek's drop-off, fine for the car). Trail mix with almonds and dark chocolate is fine (no peanuts, almonds are tree nuts not peanuts). Rice crackers with hummus is fine for everyone.
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 5 snacks against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: String cheese sticks are problematic for Sam (milk protein allergy — cheese contains casein). Whey protein bars are problematic for Sam (whey is a milk protein, his allergy specifically includes whey). Sourdough pretzels are fine for everyone in the car but must be gluten-free if included in Derek's drop-off (celiac disease). Trail mix with almonds and dark chocolate is fine — almonds are tree nuts, not peanuts, so Maya's peanut allergy is not triggered. Rice crackers with hummus is fine for everyone.
required_elements: String cheese sticks are problematic for Sam because of his milk protein allergy (cheese contains casein/milk protein)
Whey protein bars are problematic for Sam because whey is a milk protein and his allergy specifically covers whey and casein
Sourdough pretzels contain gluten — agent notes this is relevant for Derek's drop-off portion since he has celiac disease
Trail mix with almonds and dark chocolate is fine — agent confirms almonds are not peanuts and Maya's peanut allergy is not triggered
Rice crackers with hummus is fine for everyone currently in the group
forbidden_elements: Flagging trail mix as problematic for Maya (almonds are tree nuts, NOT peanuts — her allergy is specifically peanuts)
Saying Sam only needs to avoid lactose (his constraint was upgraded to full milk protein allergy)
Treating sourdough pretzels as problematic for the car group (Derek is no longer in the car, only needs gluten-free for his drop-off)
Flagging any item for Priya based on meat/fish/egg content when none of the listed items contain those (all items are vegetarian-compatible)
Saying Derek cannot come so his constraints don't matter at all (he still needs a drop-off)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests constraint UPGRADE tracking and entity lifecycle management. Key challenges: (1) Sam's constraint is upgraded from lactose intolerance to full milk protein allergy mid-conversation — the agent must apply the BROADER constraint (whey and casein, not just lactose) at probe time. String cheese and whey bars both fail under milk protein allergy but would have been partially acceptable under mere lactose intolerance (some aged cheeses are low-lactose). (2) Derek exits the trip but still needs a drop-off — his celiac/gluten constraint persists for his portion only, not for the car group. Sourdough pretzels are fine for the car but not for Derek's bag. (3) Maya joins late with an inferential constraint (EpiPen + peanut scare → peanut allergy). The trail mix contains almonds (tree nuts), NOT peanuts — this is the over-generalization trap. Almonds ≠ peanuts. (4) Priya's Jain vegetarian constraint is active but none of the probe items contain meat/fish/eggs, so nothing is flagged for her — testing that the agent doesn't over-apply constraints.

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
